article_blocks.text: Strain Type: 80% Indica / 10% Sativa / 10% Ruderalis
Genetics: Mango × Big Bang Auto
Breeder: Green House Seed Co.
THC Content: 15–20%
CBD Content: 1.25%
Terpene Profile: Myrcene , Limonene , Caryophyllene
Primary Flavors: Ripe Mango, Tropical Fruit, Sweet Citrus
Flowering Time (Indoor): 7 Weeks
Outdoor Harvest Time: 9 Weeks From Germination
Indoor Yield: 400–700 g/m²
Outdoor Yield: 60–80 g Per Plant
Grow Difficulty: Easy

A ripe mango has an unmistakable fragrance, but its appeal comes from more than sweetness. Beneath the tropical perfume is a bright, almost tart quality that keeps the flavor from becoming one-dimensional. Sweet Mango Auto captures a similar contrast in cannabis form. Developed by Green House Seed Co., this autoflowering marijuana strain combines a fruity Mango parent with Big Bang Auto to produce aromatic, resinous flowers on a relatively compact plant. Its appeal is not limited to flavor.

With a short growing cycle, strong lateral branching, and an indica-dominant experience, the cultivar offers a practical combination of convenience and character. The plant is capable of completing its life cycle without seasonal light changes, making it particularly interesting for growers working with limited time or space. An award-winning entry in the breeder’s autoflowering collection, Sweet Mango Auto demonstrates how tropical flavor and old-school cannabis genetics can work together in a fast-finishing variety.
Genetics and Lineage

Sweet Mango Auto was created by crossing Mango with Big Bang Auto, combining the aromatic qualities of a fruit-forward cannabis variety with established autoflowering genetics. Green House Seed Co. describes the resulting cultivar as approximately 80% indica, 10% sativa, and 10% ruderalis. The ruderalis component is important because it allows flowering to begin according to plant development rather than requiring the shorter daylight periods that trigger flowering in photoperiod marijuana. This trait gives the hybrid its automatic growth cycle while preserving much of the larger, resin-producing structure associated with its traditional cannabis ancestry.

The Mango parent contributes the characteristic tropical fragrance and sweet-sour flavor that define the finished flowers. Mango-named cannabis genetics have appeared in several breeding programs, but the exact deeper ancestry of the particular Mango selection used in this cross is not fully documented. Its most recognizable contribution is therefore aromatic rather than genealogical: ripe fruit sweetness, a slightly acidic edge, and a softer herbal background. The breeder’s selection aimed to retain these characteristics in a plant capable of completing a comparatively short life cycle.

Big Bang Auto supplies the other half of the breeding equation. Its background includes Skunk , Northern Lights , El Niño , and ruderalis genetics. Skunk contributes vigorous development and a recognizable traditional cannabis foundation, while Northern Lights is associated with compact growth, resin production, and substantial physical effects. El Niño adds another layer of established hybrid ancestry. The ruderalis influence provides the automatic flowering behavior. Together, these lines help explain why Sweet Mango Auto retains the relaxing qualities of an indica-dominant strain without requiring the extended cultivation schedule typical of many photoperiod varieties.
Effects and Experience

The experience tends to develop around physical comfort rather than intense stimulation. An initial sense of ease may become noticeable as muscular tension feels less prominent and ordinary activities take on a more relaxed pace. The mental effects are generally mellow, with some consumers experiencing a pleasant uplift in mood before the heavier bodily sensations become established. Rather than producing a sharp, energetic rush, the hybrid usually encourages a slower rhythm. Familiar entertainment, music, or a quiet evening may become more appealing as the effects progress.

Physical relaxation often becomes more pronounced during the middle portion of the experience. The breeder characterizes the high as long-lasting and strongly indica-oriented, particularly at larger doses. A comfortable heaviness may spread through the limbs, and the desire to remain seated can increase. Although the fruity fragrance may suggest a mild marijuana variety, its reported THC levels are substantial enough to produce significant intoxication. Experienced consumers may find moderate amounts manageable, while beginners can experience impaired concentration, slower reactions, or unexpected sedation from comparatively small servings.

Individual responses depend on more than genetics. THC concentration, tolerance, consumption method, recent food intake, and personal sensitivity all influence the experience. Higher doses can produce dry mouth, red eyes, dizziness, anxiety, or temporary difficulty with memory and coordination. Anyone unfamiliar with this cultivar should begin cautiously and allow the initial effects to develop before taking more. Edible cannabis requires particular patience because its onset is slower and its effects can persist for several hours. Driving or operating machinery while impaired is unsafe, even when the experience feels calm rather than overwhelming.
Medical Benefits

The relaxing character of Sweet Mango Auto may interest medical cannabis patients looking for help with certain forms of physical discomfort or stress-related symptoms. THC interacts with the endocannabinoid system, which participates in pain processing, appetite, mood, and other physiological functions. Research involving cannabinoid-based treatments suggests possible modest benefits for some chronic pain conditions, although findings remain mixed and the effects are not consistent across patients. Importantly, evidence about THC-containing treatments does not establish that this particular marijuana strain is effective for any specific condition.

Some individuals may appreciate the cultivar’s relatively settled mental character when discomfort makes relaxation difficult. Others may find that cannabis increases appetite or produces sleepiness later in the experience. However, these responses cannot be guaranteed. THC may also worsen anxiety, cause disorientation, or interfere with sleep quality when used frequently. Although the breeder has reported CBD in the low single-digit range, the strain remains predominantly THC-driven. Its cannabidiol content should not be assumed to offset intoxication or prevent adverse reactions.

Medical consumers should consider the potential for medication interactions, tolerance, dependence, and effects on cardiovascular or psychiatric health. Cannabis is not an appropriate substitute for prescribed treatment without professional guidance. Anyone managing a chronic condition should discuss THC use with a qualified healthcare professional and review current laboratory results whenever available. Consistent dosing and careful monitoring of personal responses are more useful than assuming a particular strain will reliably produce a desired therapeutic outcome.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

The defining sensory feature is a combination of ripe tropical fruit and noticeable acidity. Freshly opened flowers may release an aroma reminiscent of mango flesh, followed by a sharper, citrus-like note that prevents the sweetness from becoming heavy. Beneath those brighter impressions sits a mild earthy quality inherited from the cultivar’s traditional cannabis background. During flowering, the fragrance can become particularly noticeable as the plant develops dense clusters of resin-coated buds. The resulting smell has more complexity than a simple candy-like mango description might suggest.

Myrcene, limonene, and caryophyllene are commonly associated with the aromatic character described for this cultivar, although their precise concentrations are not fixed across harvests. Myrcene can contribute herbal, musky, and fruity nuances and is also naturally present in mangoes. Limonene is associated with bright citrus aromas, while beta-caryophyllene can introduce peppery and woody qualities. These compounds provide a useful framework for understanding the fragrance, but flavor descriptions cannot establish an exact terpene composition. Environmental conditions, plant selection, drying, and storage all influence the finished chemical profile.

When consumed, the flavor often begins with a rounded tropical sweetness before revealing a mildly sour finish. Some examples display additional notes of citrus peel, green herbs, or earthy spice. The fruity character is usually more noticeable in well-cured flower that has been protected from excessive heat and oxygen. Improper drying can leave a harsh grassy impression, while prolonged exposure to light may reduce delicate aromatic compounds. Careful storage helps retain the sweet-acidic balance that gives the variety its identity.
Growing Information

Sweet Mango Auto is a feminized autoflowering cultivar with a relatively compact growth habit and an energetic pattern of side-branch development. Green House Seed Co. lists a typical height of approximately 70–100 centimeters, with many plants reaching around 90 centimeters under favorable conditions. Its structure can appear more elongated than that of extremely compact autoflowers because the lateral branches develop quickly and extend outward from the central stem. As flowering progresses, long, dense buds form across these branches. A heavy coating of trichomes can give mature flowers an almost white appearance, making resin production one of the plant’s most noticeable visual characteristics.

Unlike photoperiod cannabis, this hybrid does not require a change to a 12-hour light and 12-hour dark schedule to initiate flowering. The breeder identifies approximately seven weeks of flowering and a total life cycle of around nine weeks from germination under suitable conditions. This distinction is important: the flowering period and the complete seed-to-harvest period are not the same measurement. Autoflowering plants also have a relatively brief vegetative stage, leaving less time to recover from severe stress. Gentle training, consistent watering, healthy root development , and moderate nutrition are generally more appropriate than aggressive pruning or repeated transplanting. Adequate lighting helps maintain compact growth, as insufficient light may encourage unnecessary stretching.

The breeder describes the cultivar as relatively resistant to common fungal problems, although no marijuana plant is immune to mold. Air circulation and humidity management become particularly important when dense flowers reach maturity. Indoors, published breeder figures range from approximately 400 grams per square meter in descriptive growing guidance to higher maximum estimates approaching 700 grams per square meter under optimized conditions. Outdoor production is more modest on a per-plant basis, commonly described as reaching approximately 60–80 grams in favorable environments. Because the plant flowers automatically, outdoor growers can schedule crops during suitable warm periods rather than waiting for autumn’s naturally shorter days. Nevertheless, cold weather, prolonged rain, and insufficient sunlight can still reduce yield and flower quality.

Sweet Mango Auto also has a notable competition result. It earned third place in the Best Autoflowering category at Expogrow-Irun in 2015, reflecting its established position among the earlier generations of fruit-focused automatic cannabis varieties .
FAQ
Is Sweet Mango Auto an indica or sativa strain?

Sweet Mango Auto is an indica-dominant autoflowering hybrid. Green House Seed Co. classifies it as approximately 80% indica, 10% sativa, and 10% ruderalis. Its effects generally emphasize physical relaxation and a mellow mood rather than strong stimulation. The ruderalis ancestry enables automatic flowering.
What are the genetics of Sweet Mango Auto?

The confirmed genetic cross is Mango × Big Bang Auto. The Mango parent contributes tropical fruit flavors, while Big Bang Auto brings genetics associated with Skunk, Northern Lights, El Niño, and ruderalis. This combination produces an aromatic indica-dominant plant that flowers according to age rather than seasonal daylight changes.
How much THC does Sweet Mango Auto contain?

Published figures for the cultivar vary, with breeder material describing levels ranging from the mid-teens to approximately 19.70% THC. The current composition of an individual batch depends on genetics, growing conditions, and harvest processing. Despite its sweet flavor, it can produce substantial intoxication and should be approached cautiously by inexperienced consumers.
How long does Sweet Mango Auto take from seed to harvest?

The breeder estimates approximately nine weeks for the complete growth cycle under suitable conditions, with roughly seven weeks spent flowering. Actual timing can vary depending on temperature, lighting, plant health, and phenotype. Growers should inspect mature flowers rather than relying exclusively on the number of days since germination.
Is Sweet Mango Auto suitable for beginner growers?

Its automatic flowering cycle, manageable height, and relatively resilient growth make it accessible to beginners. However, autoflowers have limited recovery time because their vegetative stage is short. Maintaining steady environmental conditions and avoiding unnecessary stress are especially important. A healthy start generally contributes more to success than complicated training methods.
Final Thoughts on Sweet Mango Auto

Sweet Mango Auto combines tropical fragrance with the practical advantages of autoflowering cannabis genetics. Its Mango and Big Bang Auto ancestry produces a compact but vigorous plant, resin-rich flowers, and a sweet-sour flavor profile that remains distinctive among fruit-oriented weed strains .

For consumers, the main attractions are its pronounced mango aroma and long-lasting, body-centered relaxation. For growers, the short life cycle and manageable structure provide flexibility without sacrificing traditional cannabis character. Its 2015 Expogrow-Irun recognition also gives the variety a place in the development of modern autoflowering breeding. Sweet Mango Auto remains an appealing example of how established indica genetics can be adapted into a fast-finishing, flavorful marijuana cultivar.
